components.label: The attributions: memory, perforator, contemplative maps
components.note: VASO-C021 is held on hypothesis statements (VASO-E013, VASO-E038) and fails the write–store–read test (VASO-E017); VASO-C174 is anchor-only in a source the ledger has not read; VASO-C022 has one uncited assertion about map locations (VASO-E039) and no blinded coding.

researchPriority.reason: Three specified accounts make different predictions about the same unfilmed seconds, and the deciding experiments — the keystone imaging (VASO-R001), the breath-randomised repeat of an already-published compression protocol (VASO-R020), the surface laser-speckle test (VASO-R016) — are cheap, unrun, and decisive in either direction; the census that would settle how common the points are (VASO-R002, VASO-R010) has never been attempted.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on hypothesis statements — Johnson's three hypotheses (VASO-E013) and the essay's relay of the clinging identification (VASO-E038) — and one qualifying record: VASO-E017 argues that hysteresis is not memory until a write–store–read loop with content-specific readout is shown, and that the only living flow network shown to store and read back information is a slime mold. Its dependencies VASO-C010 and VASO-C012 are credible but predicted by ordinary physiology; nothing admitted connects a vascular state to a later neural readout carrying information.

treatment.plainLanguage: The tension in blood-vessel walls is a kind of memory that takes part in thinking, and what Buddhism calls clinging is that grip felt from inside.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Nothing admitted tests it. A history-specific neural bias under clamped oxygenation (VASO-R005) would move the case decisively; a clean null would collapse the strong form to ordinary neurovascular physiology.
treatment.strongestObjection: A thermostat has hysteresis and no autobiography: the latch literature shows economical force maintenance, not a state that depends on prior input, is later read out, and discriminates between inputs (VASO-E017).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: In an animal preparation, different induced vascular states producing reliably different later neural responses under identical stimulation with oxygenation clamped (VASO-R005)
Vascular manipulation altering neural gain only through instantaneous perfusion, with no history dependence once perfusion is equalised — closing the strong form

claimAssessments.reasoning: Where the thesis names its compartment the record leans against it: pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles show maintained or rising myosin phosphorylation with maintained constriction (VASO-E020), no arteriole's holding cost has been measured (VASO-E019), and the critical report finds no study identifying a smooth-muscle latch at any tender point (VASO-E016). The Doppler pattern near trigger points is compatible with contracture compressing the bed as much as with distal constriction, on the imaging authors' own list (VASO-E027, weighed at zero diagnosticity). The proponent's relocation to cutaneous perforators (VASO-E044, VASO-E045) rests on an unread source and is treated as absent. No time-resolved record exists in either direction, and the arteriole studies held their stimulus on and could not have seen input-free persistence, so the verdict is unresolved rather than contradicted.

treatment.plainLanguage: A knot is a small blood vessel inside the muscle locked shut by its own smooth muscle, starving the tissue around it — a state the body maintains, not a scar.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: This is the thesis in the form the case grades; its truth or falsity decides the case against guarding-and-densification and against the perforator relocation.
treatment.strongestObjection: The only direct arteriole measurements available show sustained activation, the opposite signature to an economical dephosphorylated hold, and the stiff regions and flow patterns at trigger points are explained by contracted fibre compressing the bed without any vascular memory.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A pressurized skeletal-muscle arteriole holding constriction after stimulus withdrawal at falling phosphorylation and measured low energetic cost (VASO-R004)
Time-resolved imaging of a release with perfusion rising before stiffness falls, at palpated but not sham sites (VASO-R001)
A stiff, electrically active knot that is metabolically cold on FDG-PET (VASO-R013)
Against it: elevated FDG uptake, stiffness dropping with no perfusion change, or the non-latching motor-protein phenotype throughout skeletal-muscle arterioles

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone in SRC-JHONG-2026A, a source the ledger has not been able to read; no admitted evidence record bears on it in either direction. Its component propositions — vessel tone, a hyaluronan collar, a fascial tether, each with hysteresis — are catalogued as the essay states them, not as findings.

treatment.plainLanguage: On the perforator picture, what holds a knot is three things stacked — the vessel's tone, a collar of gelled lubricant around the bundle, and the tether that collar makes to the fascial sheet — each of which stays put after the input that set it has gone.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It is the mechanism of the second vascular account and would replace the latch as the memory element; nothing admitted tests it, so it currently decides nothing.
treatment.strongestObjection: The stiff regions blinded sonographers report lie inside the muscle in the trapezius and the calf, not in the fascia under the skin, and the whole account rests on one unread, AI-generated essay.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Blinded tender points coinciding with pencil-Doppler perforators above chance (VASO-R015)
A knot released by saline hydrodissection at its perforator with no breath (VASO-R017)
Tender points falling on perforators no more often than chance

claimAssessments.reasoning: The only record in either direction is the founding essay's uncited assertion that traditional maps place the important knots along the torso's midline and limbs (VASO-E039), with no coding rule and no chance baseline; the blinded pre-registered coding the critical report requires (VASO-R006) has not been done.

treatment.plainLanguage: The knots and channels of Tibetan, Indian and Chinese contemplative anatomy are maps of the same tension system, drawn from the inside by trained attention.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Even a genuine alignment with vascular geography would not show that anything latches or clenches; a failed alignment would only retire the convergence argument.
treatment.strongestObjection: Correspondence found after the fact is the weakest kind of evidence; without pre-specified coding every match is vulnerable to post-hoc fitting.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Blind coding of rtsa mdud, granthi and ashi locations aligning with perforators, sympathetic chains or dorsal root ganglia better than chance
The same coding finding alignment no better than chance

claimAssessments.reasoning: Hai and Murphy's kinetic model reproduces sustained stress at low myosin phosphorylation in smooth-muscle preparations (VASO-E003, strong); the essay's restatement (VASO-E034) adds nothing and overstates the model as force at zero activation. The study table qualifies generality: latch behaviour was present in the rabbit femoral artery and absent one branch order later in its saphenous branch, and never followed downstream (VASO-E021).

treatment.plainLanguage: Smooth muscle in vessel walls can lock its grip and hold tension cheaply after the signal that started it fades.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Textbook physiology that every account accepts; it makes the vascular hypothesis possible without making it likely, and it has not been shown in the vessels a knot would need.
treatment.strongestObjection: The capability is demonstrated in conduit arteries; the one comparison across a branch order lost it, so vascular smooth muscle does not generically latch (VASO-E021).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A paired-caliber study finding the non-latching phenotype throughout skeletal-muscle arterioles, narrowing the claim to conduit vessels
Latch behaviour demonstrated in pressurized arterioles, extending it to the compartment the thesis needs

claimAssessments.reasoning: Graded on physiological priors, disclosed here: structural remodelling takes days to weeks, so a change completing in seconds is a change of maintained state. The ledger holds the argument as the essay states it (VASO-E035) and, as context, a pilot in which needled points shrank over visits (VASO-E030). Its premise — an objective local event within seconds — is the unmeasured thing; the nearest admitted observation, an imaged focus becoming undetectable over minutes of compression, sits on sibling VASO-C005 (VASO-E072) and is named as such.

treatment.plainLanguage: If a knot really lets go in seconds, whatever let go was something the body was doing, not scar tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It rules out scar if its premise holds, but 'state' includes guarding and fascial densification as well as vessels, so it does not decide between the three accounts.
treatment.strongestObjection: No time-resolved record shows any objective change within seconds; and even a fast change would be equally predicted by guarding switching off or hyaluronan thinning.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved elastography and Doppler showing a stiffness drop within seconds of an exhale (VASO-R001)
Felt releases with no reproducible local transition, which would remove the premise

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone (the founding essay, p. 3) with no admitted evidence record; the Stecco-group primaries were sought and not retrieved. The reversal timescale, which is what would make it a competitor to the vascular accounts, has not entered the ledger.

treatment.plainLanguage: Thickened fascial lubricant thins again under pressure, movement and warmth.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If densification reverses in seconds, the knot could be a state without being a vessel and pressure alone should work; if it takes hours, the vascular accounts remain the only candidates for a seconds-scale release. The timescale has not been retrieved (VASO-R008).
treatment.strongestObjection: Held on the essay's word; the critical report notes the densification literature is anatomical and mechanistic rather than a demonstration at any painful point, and that a quantitative hyaluronan study found no simple age effect.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A retrieved primary giving a measured reversal timescale under load and warmth
Fascial densification reversing under pressure with no perfusion change in the keystone rig

claimAssessments.reasoning: Moore and Cao proposed it (VASO-E004, context); Jammal Salameh and colleagues showed blood-pressure pulsations modulating central neurons through mechanosensitive channels in rat preparations and awake animals (VASO-E005, strong). That is instantaneous modulation in brain — not storage, not content-specific readout, not the periphery — hence provisional for the claim as the case uses it.

treatment.plainLanguage: The state of nearby blood vessels can change what neurons do, not just feed them.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It supplies the read path the synthesis needs, but ordinary neurovascular physiology now includes it; it says nothing about knots or memory.
treatment.strongestObjection: A vessel nudging a neuron now is not a vessel storing anything; the demonstration is in rat cortex, not around a tender point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Peripheral sensory endings shown to change firing with arteriolar caliber in situ
The VASO-R005 experiment separating history-dependent from instantaneous effects

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review of slow-breathing studies in healthy humans documents reproducible rises in heart-rate variability and respiratory sinus arrhythmia (VASO-E009, strong); the essay's restatement (VASO-E036) adds nothing. The measures are global cardiovascular indices; no local tissue or tender-point measurement exists.

treatment.plainLanguage: Breathing slowly, especially breathing out long, reliably tips the nervous system toward its rest-and-digest side.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Every account grants it; it establishes a global shift measured on the heart in people with no tender point in the study, not a local key.
treatment.strongestObjection: It is measured on the heart, globally; nothing shows it unlatching or reopening any particular vessel.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A local, site-specific vascular change time-locked to exhalation, which would make the lever local as well as global
Failure of slow breathing to shift HRV in a large preregistered sample — not expected

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review found manual examination not demonstrated reliable or valid and lacking a reference standard (VASO-E011, strong); the Quintner–Bove–Cohen critique disputes the construct itself (VASO-E010), answered but not settled; proponent groups concede the point in their own words (VASO-E029, VASO-E078, VASO-E079) and one reports imaging confirmed 71.5% of palpated spots (VASO-E081).

treatment.plainLanguage: Examiners do not reliably agree where trigger points are, there is no agreed test for what one is, and whether the construct is real is disputed in the literature.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It caps every account equally — all locate their object by palpation — and it is why the keystone design requires blinded instrumented localization.
treatment.strongestObjection: Instrumented findings at palpated sites — stiffness gradients from blinded sonographers — show something is there even if the thumb is unreliable; the critique targets the manual exam and the classic taut-band construct, not tenderness itself.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A validated instrumented reference standard with demonstrated inter-examiner reliability
Imaging-anchored localisation reproducing the palpated classification blind

claimAssessments.reasoning: The claim bundles two propositions. That discrete, exquisitely tender points occur is documented: examiners found them at fixed sites in a community general-practice sample, including in two people who reported no pain at all (VASO-E082, context, in a pain-selected subsample; VASO-E083, context), and the instrumented trigger-point studies on sibling claim VASO-C005 found them in every patient examined — a disclosed basis, not a record attached here. That they occur commonly across the general population is held on the founding essay's own report (VASO-E015, weak, proponent testimony) and a 1986 clinic estimate of myofascial pain quoted second-hand in an imaging introduction (VASO-E028, weak); no census, no unselected sample and no prevalence measurement has been admitted, and the critical report records that even the palpable discrete spot is disputed (VASO-E012). The claim as stated is therefore weakly supported: its occurrence half is observed, its frequency half is unmeasured and would be unresolved on its own. The claim should be split at intake so each half can be graded on its own records.

treatment.plainLanguage: Small, very tender spots in muscle are something most people have.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Occurrence is granted by every account; frequency across the population, if measured, would bear on the ubiquity argument for a stored-tension account but would not decide which tissue holds the state.
treatment.strongestObjection: The only population record is two individuals in a sample chosen for pain, at fixed sites the exam prescribes; the general-population frequency is the essay's word and a clinic estimate for a pain syndrome, and the reproducibility of the palpable spot itself is contested (VASO-E012).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: An unselected community sample with tender-point counts by age and sex (VASO-R010, VASO-R002)
A knot census with pain-free controls finding palpable points rare outside symptomatic muscle

claimAssessments.reasoning: Hubbard and Berkoff recorded sustained spontaneous activity in a 1–2 mm nidus of every trapezius trigger point and none in adjacent non-tender fibres (VASO-E001); Simons, Hong and Simons found endplate noise at 11 of 11 trigger-point sites, 4 of 11 non-tender endplate-zone sites and 0 of 11 off-zone taut-band sites (VASO-E031, qualifies), making the signature a prevalence gradient rather than an exclusive island. The essay restatement (VASO-E043) and the equine parallel from an unread source (VASO-E052) carry no independent weight. Old, small, one lineage each, abstract-only for Simons.

treatment.plainLanguage: Trigger points crackle with ongoing electrical activity at a tiny spot, more often than non-tender spots in the same nerve-supply band and never where there is no such band.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It shows something is actively maintained, which any state account predicts; it says where the signature lives — the endplate zone — which favours the skeletal reading over a vascular one.
treatment.strongestObjection: Endplate noise is a property of the endplate zone that trigger points share; its generator is skeletal-muscle electrophysiology on every published reading, and nothing vascular was measured.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A matched endplate-zone control site under stress rising as much as the trigger point (VASO-R011), relocating the phenomenon to endplates generally
Sympathetic blockade quieting the nidus in a retrieved primary (VASO-R009)

claimAssessments.reasoning: One record: mental arithmetic raised trigger-point EMG while control sites in the same muscle stayed comparatively quiet, in fourteen subjects from the Hubbard lineage (VASO-E002); the essay's restatement (VASO-E033) adds nothing. No matched endplate-zone control, no vascular endpoint, and the relaxation and phentolamine follow-ups remain unretrieved.

treatment.plainLanguage: Giving someone a mental arithmetic test turns up the electrical activity inside one tender point but not a centimetre away.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The write half of any storage account, but three readings fit it — stress-sensitive endplates, a sympathetic write to an arteriole, a skin-territory vasoconstriction — and the needle cannot tell them apart.
treatment.strongestObjection: The control needle may have sat off the endplate zone; sympathetic drive to spindles or endplates fits the data without any vascular element.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A repeat with a matched endplate-zone control (VASO-R011)
Skin perfusion over the point falling under arithmetic and not over control skin

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone in SRC-JHONG-2026A, a source the ledger has not read; no admitted evidence record bears on it. It is the perforator account's reading of the McNulty result, catalogued as the essay states it.

treatment.plainLanguage: The stress response at one tender point is the brain blanching a patch of skin, as in blushing.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Would separate the perforator reading of VASO-C003 from the endplate and arteriole readings; nothing admitted tests it.
treatment.strongestObjection: The signal McNulty recorded was needle EMG in muscle, not skin perfusion; nothing shows a skin-territory write at a tender point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Laser speckle over the point during arithmetic showing a localized perfusion fall and not over control skin (VASO-R016, VASO-R011)
Global or absent perfusion change under the stressor

claimAssessments.reasoning: Supported only by first-person and practitioner testimony from the hypothesis's proponent, in an essay whose text was AI-generated at the author's direction (VASO-E014, weak); consistent with widespread lore, contradicted by no one, measured by no one. Real evidence that people feel a release; none that anything happens in the tissue.

treatment.plainLanguage: Press on a knot and breathe out slowly and, within seconds, it feels like it lets go.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: As a felt event it is predicted by every account, including expectation riding global relaxation; only an objective local transition time-locked to the exhale would make it decisive, and none has been measured.
treatment.strongestObjection: Expectation and attention riding a genuine global parasympathetic shift produce felt releases without any local event; nothing has been measured.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-locked local stiffness and perfusion change at palpated but not sham sites (VASO-R001, VASO-R016)
Felt releases with no reproducible local transition, or equal transitions at shams

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor (the founding essay, p. 3); the one admitted record (VASO-E067, context) establishes that a published pressure-only protocol carried no breathing instruction, recording or manipulation, and nothing more. What that protocol achieved — 60% of active and 86% of latent imaged points undetectable after one round of minutes-long compression — is held on VASO-C005 (VASO-E072) and is named here as a lead against the two-key rule, an inference across claims and not a grade: breathing was uninstructed, not held constant, and a runner under painful pressure may exhale slowly unbidden.

treatment.plainLanguage: Pressure alone will not release a knot; it takes the breath as well.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If false, the breath is a felt correlate and the cleanest argument that the released element answers to autonomic state goes with it; if true, breath-gating is real and both vascular accounts gain.
treatment.strongestObjection: The one published pressure-only protocol cleared most imaged points with nobody told how to breathe.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Pressure during an inhale-and-hold failing to clear points that pressure during free breathing clears (VASO-R020)
Equal clearance under held breath, slow exhalation and free breathing, all exceeding sham
A knot released by hydrodissection with no breath at all (VASO-R017)

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor alone (the founding essay, p. 31) with no admitted evidence record; it is the prediction both vascular accounts make and no rival makes, and no time-resolved measurement exists in either direction.

treatment.plainLanguage: When a knot releases, blood comes back before the tissue softens.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The one timing prediction that separates the vascular accounts from guarding and densification; untested, so it currently carries the case's sharpest test rather than any weight.
treatment.strongestObjection: No time-resolved measurement exists; guarding and densification predict a stiffness change with no local perfusion change, and that has not been tested either.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Perfusion leading stiffness across events in VASO-R001 or VASO-R016
Stiffness leading, simultaneous change, or no local perfusion change

claimAssessments.reasoning: Biochemistry from Shah 2008 in about nine volunteers, elevated at remote as well as near sites (VASO-E006); the Mazza review, second-hand (VASO-E007); Ballyns 2011's group-level Doppler difference (VASO-E022) and blinded vibration-elastography stiff-area gradient (VASO-E087, VASO-E090, VASO-E091, VASO-E092, VASO-E096, VASO-E099, VASO-E100, VASO-E102), capped by no pain-free controls (VASO-E026) and flow indices that cannot classify sites (VASO-E025); Landfald 2025's active-versus-latent differences in the calf as context and qualifier (VASO-E068, VASO-E069, VASO-E070, VASO-E071, VASO-E072). The second-essay restatements (VASO-E050, VASO-E051) rest on an unread source and are treated as absent. Group-level differences are real; every comparison sits inside symptomatic muscle at palpation-selected sites.

treatment.plainLanguage: Where an examiner finds a trigger point, the tissue really does measure differently — more acid, stiffer, different blood flow.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: All three accounts predict measurable local differences; the vascular signature is partial, and nothing here says what the stiff tissue is.
treatment.strongestObjection: Every comparison sits inside symptomatic muscle at palpation-selected sites from a lineage that also produced the biochemistry; one Doppler index shows no difference and the other cannot classify a site.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A census with pain-free controls and instrument-fixed sites finding Doppler and stiffness do not pick out palpated spots
Independent replication of the stiffness gradient with pain-free controls and blinded site selection

claimAssessments.reasoning: One strong record from a single laboratory: preregistered within-subject experiments in 57 volunteers, ~1.5-fold smaller and faster-resolving histamine responses under inward attention with no arousal difference (VASO-E008); the essay relays the authors' caveat that the route is vagal and skin is not parasympathetically innervated (VASO-E041). Provisional because single-lab and very recent.

treatment.plainLanguage: Paying attention to an inflamed spot on your skin makes the inflammation smaller and shorter, without changing arousal.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: An existence proof that cognition can write to a peripheral vascular bed at a chosen site; it says nothing about knots, smooth muscle or seconds.
treatment.strongestObjection: The route is vagal immune regulation over about twenty minutes in healthy skin, in a tissue the parasympathetic system does not directly innervate; nothing latches or unlatches.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication, or failure, of the histamine-attention effect
An attention effect on local perfusion at a tender point within seconds

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 reports a median pulsatility index of 8.3 near active sites against 3.0 near palpably normal sites (VASO-E022), in pulsatile arteries typically over a millimetre across, 1–2 cm from the point; there was no pain-free control group and the authors say the findings do not represent normal variation (VASO-E026).

treatment.plainLanguage: Arteries near painful trigger points pulse more sharply than arteries near normal spots in the same muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Compatible with a throttled bed and equally with contracture squeezing it, on the authors' own list; conduit-scale vessels, not the microvessels a latch account needs.
treatment.strongestObjection: Large variance, no pain-free controls, and the index could not classify any individual site.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Replication with pain-free controls and microvascular Doppler
The difference vanishing when transducer pressure and contracture are controlled

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 reports retrograde diastolic flow near 15 of 48 palpably normal sites (31%) against 55% of active sites (VASO-E022); the normal sites lay 5 cm from a trigger point in symptomatic muscle, so the source cannot say whether 31% is baseline or spillover (VASO-E026).

treatment.plainLanguage: Blood runs briefly backward between heartbeats near about a third of spots that feel normal in a muscle that has trigger points elsewhere.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It makes the waveform a gradient across symptomatic muscle rather than a marker of a knot, undercutting the footprint reading whichever account is right.
treatment.strongestObjection: 'Normal' sites were 5 cm from trigger points in symptomatic patients, so the 31% may be spillover or baseline; the source cannot say.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: The retrograde-flow rate at matched sites in pain-free controls
A gradient of retrograde flow with distance from the point

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 reports mean areas of 0.57 ± 0.20 cm² at active and 0.36 ± 0.16 cm² at latent sites on vibration sonoelastography (VASO-E087, VASO-E089), with the active-versus-latent significance and ROC separation as context (VASO-E093, VASO-E106) and the calf active/latent size difference as a parallel from another muscle and method (VASO-E085). Blinded sonographers, one laboratory, one vibration frequency, palpation-selected sites, same NIH lineage as the biochemistry.

treatment.plainLanguage: On stiffness imaging, painful trigger points cover a larger stiff area (about 0.57 cm²) than ones that hurt only when pressed (about 0.36 cm²).
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A graded stiffness inside the muscle is what any account predicts; it locates the stiff tissue in muscle rather than under skin, which weighs slightly against the perforator picture.
treatment.strongestObjection: Sites were chosen by palpation and the classification presupposed; single vibration frequency from an off-the-shelf massager, single lab.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication with shear-wave elastography and blinded site selection
Failure to reproduce the active/latent ordering

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 reports 0.17 ± 0.22 cm² at palpably normal sites, significantly below both classes of trigger point (VASO-E090), with the overall ROC separation and the active-versus-normal and latent-versus-normal classifiers carrying the comparison (VASO-E104, VASO-E105, VASO-E107). The normal sites lay in symptomatic muscle and the standard deviation exceeds the mean.

treatment.plainLanguage: Spots that feel normal in the same muscle show a small stiff area too, about 0.17 cm², below both classes of trigger point.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: It anchors the gradient's bottom rung, but in symptomatic muscle without pain-free controls, so the true normal value is unknown.
treatment.strongestObjection: 'Normal' here means 5 cm from a trigger point in a painful neck; the standard deviation exceeds the mean.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Normal-site areas measured in pain-free controls
Replication across vibration frequencies and with shear-wave elastography

claimAssessments.reasoning: Simons, Hong and Simons report endplate noise at 4 of 11 non-tender endplate-zone sites against 11 of 11 trigger-point sites (VASO-E032); abstract only, nonrandomized, unblinded, ten subjects, authors the construct's leading proponents.

treatment.plainLanguage: The same electrical crackle shows up at some non-tender spots in the nerve-supply band, though less often.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Cuts against exclusivity of the nidus and supports the endplate reading of VASO-C002; it dictates which control the stressor experiment needs.
treatment.strongestObjection: Small, unblinded, abstract only; per-site amplitudes unrecorded.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Blinded replication with per-site amplitudes
Endplate-zone controls found silent under matched recording

claimAssessments.reasoning: Simons, Hong and Simons report no endplate noise at any of 11 taut-band sites outside the endplate zone (VASO-E032); same design limits as VASO-C034.

treatment.plainLanguage: Taut bands away from the nerve-supply band show no such crackle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Places the signature in the endplate zone first and the trigger point second — the skeletal-endplate reading — and suggests Hubbard–Berkoff's silent controls may have lain off the zone.
treatment.strongestObjection: Small, unblinded, abstract only.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Spontaneous activity recorded at off-zone taut-band sites in a blinded replication
Hubbard–Berkoff's control sites shown to have lain within the endplate zone

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 reports no difference in resistivity index between active, latent and normal sites (VASO-E024); a negative recorded in its own right, within symptomatic patients, which the authors attribute partly to proximity of normal sites to trigger points.

treatment.plainLanguage: One standard measure of downstream flow resistance is the same near painful, latent and normal spots.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A negative in its own right: the vascular signature at trigger points is partial, not categorical.
treatment.strongestObjection: Normal sites near trigger points may share their downstream bed, so the null may be proximity rather than absence of a difference.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Resistivity differences emerging against pain-free controls
Microvascular indices differing where conduit resistivity does not
